significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that scFM representations obey the measurable relation that "direct edges will survive representational conditioning on mediators while indirect edges will vanish," with mediator clamping selectively blocking indirect perturbation propagation; this is a form-(iii) conditional-independence law coupled to a causal-mechanism claim. It would fix expectations for unseen regulatory cascades and materially constrain whether network and perturbation interpretations of systems such as Geneformer (Theodoris et al., Nature 2023) and scGPT (Cui et al., Nature Methods 2024) are defensible: CISI supplies the representational phenomenon, while mediation-blocking supplies the load-bearing mechanism. Verified false and above-baseline marginal signal would rule out this specific d-separation account, although it would not make the claimed "decisive" case for pure co-expression because other mechanistic encodings remain possible and a null perturbation result is explicitly treated as head-limited; nevertheless, true and false are distinguishable states. In the topic-substitution check, replacing the direct-versus-mediated law with the generic question of whether scientific mechanisms are represented would merit only the topic median, so the uplift comes from this claim's specific ordering and intervention consequences.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Conditional-Independence Selectivity Index (CISI)" and "Mediation-Blocking Asymmetry (MBA)," which can be used to audit an scFM before treating it as a mechanistic prior for perturbation-guided discovery, giving limited ex-ante lead time rather than merely explaining a completed failure. After re-extraction on another model, the conclusion predicts relations—direct-pair conditioned association should exceed indirect-pair association and MBA should be positive—rather than merely supplying an open-ended procedure for finding a new direction. The asserted scope covers pretrained scFMs, multiple regulatory cascades, and cell types, with downstream uptake by model auditors and biological researchers deciding whether to use these models for regulatory inference, but it remains confined to gene-regulatory mediation rather than supplying a general scientific-mechanism audit. Under topic substitution, the generic topic provides neither CISI nor the predicted direct-versus-mediated inequality, so this reach score is attributable to the claim rather than to biology's general importance.
